title: His father's band and its members
summary: Handy names the men in his father's band, himself on drums, and its Gulfport hotel job paying $35-40 a week.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Who was in your daddy's band? Did he have a band of his own or what?

Yeah, he had a band of his own. He had a fellow by the name of Joe Davis playing guitar. A fellow by the name of Selby Thomas on, uh, bass. Uh, uh, what's his trumpet player name? Uh, Moulier Melanson. He was on trumpet. And, uh, I was on drums. My cousin was playing drums before. I got big enough to play drums. And his name? Charlie Watson. And, uh, who else? At that time, they wasn't usually getting, I mean, no piano. And then... Trombone? Well, trombone and a fellow by the name of, uh, Frank Toes playing trombone.

As a matter of fact, his son's playing trombone somewhere around Memphis. Do you know his son's name? They call him Wash. I don't know his other name. All I know is Wash. Did you name a clarinet player with your father's family? No. No, he didn't have one?

He had a fallout of Basin who used to call Summer of the Bot. Used to play with him a lot. He had another fallout of Basin who used to play with him too, but I forget his name. They used to do the Ice Wake that one. I remember when he was playing at the Great Southern Hotel there in Gulfport. Playing out there on Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sundays. And they was making around $35, $40 a week. And that was pretty good money in them days. Yeah, it was a nice having those days.
